actions.description: Cut cedar from the Oregon forest into logs.
Take logs from the logger and saw them into pencil slats.
Take graphite from the mine and mix it with clay to form pencil leads.

Deliver the carrier's shipment to its named shop destination.
A customer buys pencils from a shop at its listed price.

mechanics.rationale: The logger cuts the stated quantity of standing cedar into logs.

checks.label: The forest has enough standing cedar

limits: Only the represented standing-cedar stock and the logger's logs change; transport and forest renewal are not represented by this move.
tests: Refuse a zero or negative quantity.

semantic_bindings: forest is the cut-cedar action's forest

mechanics.rationale: The sawmill takes the specified logs from the named logger and turns them into slats.
limits: The move does not represent transportation of logs between places.
tests: Refuse a zero or negative quantity.
Refuse when the named logger lacks the quantity; otherwise transfer that quantity from logs to sawmill slats.

mechanics.rationale: The miner mines the stated quantity of graphite into its represented stock.
limits: No mine reserve is represented, so its depletion cannot be tracked or checked.
tests: Refuse a zero or negative quantity.
A positive quantity increases the miner's graphite stock by that quantity.

mechanics.rationale: The lead works consumes the stated quantity of graphite and clay and makes that quantity of leads.

checks.label: The lead works has enough clay

limits: Graphite and clay are consumed one unit per lead; no additional mixing ratio is represented.
tests: Refuse if the mine lacks graphite or the lead works lacks clay.
When both stocks suffice, consume the quantity of each and add that quantity of leads.

mechanics.rationale: Assembly consumes slats, leads, paint, erasers, and ferrules and makes the stated quantity of pencils.

checks.label: The lead works has enough leads

limits: The represented inventory has no separate glue stock; assembly consumes one unit each of the represented slats, leads, paint, erasers, and ferrules per pencil.
tests: Refuse unless every named input stock meets the requested quantity.
On success, consume each input quantity and make the same number of pencils.
semantic_bindings: sawmill and lead_works are the named input businesses

mechanics.rationale: Packing consumes one box per pencil and reclassifies the specified quantity as packed pencils.
limits: The model treats one box as packing one pencil; box contents are not otherwise represented.
tests: Refuse if pencils or boxes are insufficient.
Otherwise consume the requested pencils and boxes and add the same quantity to packed pencils.

mechanics.rationale: The carrier takes boxed pencils from the source and starts a shipment for the named shop destination.

checks.label: The source has enough boxed pencils
The carrier has no shipment in progress
The carrier has no cargo already loaded

limits: Booking starts a one-round trip; delivery is a separate action and requires the countdown to reach zero.
tests: Refuse an insufficient source stock or an occupied carrier shipment.
On success, transfer the requested cargo and set the destination and one round remaining.
semantic_bindings: source is the factory stock source

mechanics.rationale: The carrier delivers its loaded cargo only to its named destination once the trip countdown has ended.

checks.label: The shipment destination is this shop
The carrier has cargo to deliver

limits: Delivery must be explicitly performed after the shipment countdown reaches zero; no automatic transfer is modeled.
tests: Refuse delivery to a different shop or before arrival.
After arrival, transfer all cargo to the named shop and clear the destination.
semantic_bindings: to is the action's named shop

mechanics.rationale: A purchase transfers exactly one pencil and charges the shop's listed price once, as required for priced moves.

checks.label: The customer is waiting for pencils
The shop has a pencil available
The customer can afford the listed price

limits: Each purchase sells exactly one pencil and charges the listed shop price once, regardless of the action quantity.
The model does not create a replacement waiting customer after a sale.
tests: Refuse if the customer is not waiting, the shop has no stock, or the customer cannot afford the price.
A successful purchase transfers one pencil and the listed price and reduces both represented waiting counts by one.

processes.rationale: A shipment takes time to travel; its represented rounds remaining count decreases once each round until it reaches zero.

checks.label: The shipment is on its journey

processes.rationale: New customer demand continues to arrive, as represented by the shop's waiting-customer count and the customer's waiting-for-pencils count.

checks.label: The shop's customer queue is active
